title: Potato Gnocchi with Butter-Tomato Sauce
summary: Light potato gnocchi, made from baked rather than boiled potatoes to keep them tender, served in a gentle butter-tomato sauce.
equipment: 2 baking trays dusted with flour or semolina

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper, King Edward or russet), scrubbed
plain flour, plus extra for dusting
ingredients.note: you may need 10-20 g less or more

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
tin whole plum tomatoes with their juice
fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (1%)
ingredients.note: about 6.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Make the sauce first
steps.text: Put the tomatoes, butter, onion half and salt into a saucepan and simmer uncovered over low heat for 40 minutes, crushing the tomatoes as you go. It's ready when thick and glossy; discard the onion and keep the sauce warm. The butter here softens the sauce's acidity so it stays gentle enough for delicate gnocchi.

steps.title: Bake the potatoes
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, prick the potatoes all over and bake them directly on the oven rack for 50-60 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance. Baking rather than boiling keeps the potato flesh drier, which means less flour is needed later — the real secret to light gnocchi.

steps.title: Rice the potatoes
steps.text: While still hot, halve the potatoes and scoop out the flesh, pressing it through a ricer onto the worktop in a thin, even layer. Let it stand for 5 minutes to steam off a little moisture, but work with it while it's still warm rather than letting it go fully cold.

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.text: Sprinkle the salt and egg yolk over the riced potato, then sieve over two-thirds of the flour and cut it in with a bench scraper. Gather and fold-press the mixture 4-5 times, adding the remaining flour only until it just holds together and feels barely tacky; avoid kneading or smearing it, since overworking develops gluten and makes the gnocchi rubbery rather than light.

steps.title: Test the dough
steps.text: Boil a single small piece of the dough to check it; if it falls apart in the water, fold in another 1-2 tablespoons of flour before shaping the rest. This quick test saves you from shaping a whole batch that won't hold together.

steps.title: Shape the gnocchi
steps.text: Cut the dough into 6 pieces and roll each into a 2cm rope with light hands, then cut into 2cm lengths. Roll each piece down the length of a fork or a gnocchi board to leave ridges, which help the sauce cling once cooked, then lay them on floured trays without letting them touch.

steps.title: Cook until they float
steps.text: Heat 4 litres of water with the 40g of salt to a rolling boil and boil the gnocchi in 2 batches. They're done when they float to the surface, after about 2 minutes, then give them 30 seconds more before lifting them straight into the sauce with a slotted spoon, keeping back a mug of the cooking water.

steps.title: Finish gently in the sauce
steps.text: Tip the sauce into a frying pan over low heat, add the gnocchi and 2-3 tablespoons of the cooking water, then shake the pan gently for 30-60 seconds to coat everything. Shake rather than stir hard, since the gnocchi are tender and can break apart easily. Serve with the basil and Parmesan.

tips: Bake the potatoes rather than boiling them — boiled potatoes hold extra water, which means adding far more flour and ending up with heavier gnocchi.
Work the dough as little as possible once the flour goes in; overworking develops gluten and turns gnocchi tough instead of light.
Always test-boil one piece before shaping the whole batch, so you can adjust the flour if needed.
Handle the cooked gnocchi gently in the sauce — shake the pan rather than stirring with a spoon, or they'll break apart.
storage: Shaped, uncooked gnocchi freeze well on a floured tray for up to 2 months and can be cooked straight from frozen with an extra minute. Cooked gnocchi keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently in a pan with the sauce until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
